steps.text: Early the next morning, the restaurant is still quiet, save for a few fowlbeasts jumping back and forth on the fallen leaves outside the door.
The night watchman at the Judicial Review Office lets out a loud yawn. The fowlbeasts take off in all directions.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: *Yawns* Ughh...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I had a nightmare last night that a beckbeast ate all the flour in my kitchen. How terrifying!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Morning!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Have some noodles!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You... figured out how to make them?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Look at the bags under your eyes. Were you practicing all night?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Haha. No. Only about half the night. Hey, Xingzhu still hasn't woken up yet.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Enough talking for now. Try the noodles!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You.... huh?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You gave up learning how to knead the dough and boiled some ready-made noodles instead?!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: These are no ordinary ready-made noodles. Xingzhu and I looked through all the ready-made noodles on the market, and picked the ones we feel have a texture closest to your hand-made ones.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Of course, they don't have quite the same mouthfeel as hand-made noodles. So Xingzhu adjusted your soup base recipe to ensure they taste similar to the longevity noodles you make from scratch.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: This is blasphemy! You're using ready-made noodles, and you tampered with my recipe? My word!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Don't jump to any conclusions yet. Please, have a taste!
The Young Chef picks up his chopsticks, and, with a giant frown on his face, pulls out some of the noodles. He carefully takes a sniff, then finally takes a taste.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Well...?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Say something!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Why did you two think this would work?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Xingzhu was starving after all my failed attempts! I figured at that point, I was better off just making noodles I knew how to make, so at least she'd have something to eat!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Then I started thinking: the most important element of longevity noodles isn't the taste. Instead, it's making sure the person who eats them feels the birthday blessing.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Some people just aren't skilled enough to make noodles like you do. However, I can still use ready-made noodles to bring birthday blessings to myself or my family. That's the real meaning of longevity noodles, anyway.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: See how yellow and shiny these noodles are? They look more lively than yours, right?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Of course, yes, I am taking shortcuts with this dish...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You mentioned birthday blessings. Do you think people can taste that in your noodles?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I... think so?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Last night, after I finally made a proper bowl of noodles for the first time, I shared them with Xingzhu. We felt so happy when eating it. I even caught Xingzhu wiping away tears...

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Swapping out the noodles, then adjusting the oil and salt ratios accordingly... Quite some innovation there. Xingzhu sure has a sharp palate.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: But the ready-made noodles need to be rinsed with cold water after cooking. You rinsed them, but you didn't drain all the cold water out.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: The cold water lowered the temperature of the soup, which also affected the texture of the noodles. If you really want to make good food, you need to be mindful of these little details.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Got it! I'll remember that!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Wait, then you mean...?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Enough. I'm only continuing to teach you because I can see you've put in the effort.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: You still need to learn how to make your own noodles from scratch. You don't really expect to use ready-made noodles in the competition, do you?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hehe. Great!

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: As your shifu, I'm glad that you've improved. But we still have to see whether the customers recognize your efforts.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Well... what do we do?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Later on, if anyone orders noodles, you'll make them.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: If the customer doesn't like the noodles, then you'll need to keep practicing.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I'm on it!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hello! Would you like to try our special longevity noodles?

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: It's not my birthday. Why would I want longevity noodles?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: It's a new dish we're trying out. We'll give it to you for free!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: No. I meant, if you try it, and like it, then maybe you should still pay for it. I mean, I have to settle up with the boss, you know.

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: That's... an interesting way to do business.

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: Sure. Give me that bowl of noodles, then.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: (eager eyes)

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: Uhh... do you need something else from me?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: No! No! I just want to see how you like the noodles.

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: Okay okay. I'll give them a try.
The man picks up one single noodle using his chopsticks, then a piece of bok choy, and some scallions. He tries them one after another.
He eats with graceful manners, but somehow, in just a few moments' time, the entire bowl is empty.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What do you think?

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: Mmmm... Good. Even excellent.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: R-Really?

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: The soup has a rich umami taste, and the ingredients are top notch. If you had let the soup simmer for another day or so, it might have tasted even better.

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: But I was already so hungry. If I had tried to wait another day for that ultimate perfection, I would have starved...

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: He wants to create the perfect taste, but the customer cannot wait that long.

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: Even if I want to wait for him... there are some things that I just can't wait for any longer...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You're saying...

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: Don't worry about it. Just tell your boss what I said, yeah?
The man stands up. The patterns on his clothes emit a strange glow; the light distorts and blurs his face, so much so that Blaze cannot make out what he looks like.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hey! You... you didn't pay!

steps.name: Sharp Dressed Man
steps.text: Just deduct the funds from my account.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: Regardless of what you're looking for, after you leave here, do not tell anyone you got this file from the Academy. Do you understand?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: What's wrong? Do you have more questions?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Do you remember... that bloody case... back in 1062?

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: This isn't the sort of thing you casually bring up in a conversation.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I just happened to think of it.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Is the Grand Preceptor you previously mentioned, the one who supported the academic reforms which benefited countless poor students, the same Grand Preceptor who murdered the emperor and plotted treason forty years ago?

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: I have no way to answer your question. I will never speak about things that I do not know.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: I have never met that Grand Preceptor in person, but I have read some of her writings on political and social issues. Her extensive knowledge, clearly reflected in her works, has been deeply enriching for me.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: But people are complicated and cannot be easily categorized.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You're saying you're not completely convinced that the outcome of that case was correct?

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: Qingyan, you are never good at hiding what you are thinking.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: I knew you would...

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: The Office's archives will not house muddled cases, no matter how many people they involve.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Solving those cases is my duty as deputy minister.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: I shall not dissuade you from doing as you see fit. However, you must learn to protect yourself, no matter what happens.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: *sigh* Before your parents retreated into seclusion in the mountains, they entrusted me with looking after you. If anything were to happen to you, I would never be able to look them in the eyes again.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I'm not a child. Why do I need people to take care of me?

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: Everyone feels that way when they are young. However, as a mother, watching Zuo Le grow up, day by day, I feel a weight growing on my heart.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: What else should we parents worry about, other than our children's safety?

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: But if your parents learned that I prevented you from fulfilling your duties out of concern for your 'safety', then they really would blame me.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Duoxie... Sister...

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: *sigh* You call me your sister, but in my eyes, you have always been like a child of my son's generation.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Speaking of which, Yumen is near Baizao now. Have you seen General Zuo at all over the past few days?

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: Things are coming to a head. The Ministry of War is holding meetings day and night, and the general must remain on the front lines to oversee things personally.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: Neither he nor I can abandon our posts.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: There is truly no way to avoid this conflict?

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: This isn't something I have the authority to decide.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: As an Advisor for the Ministry of War, my job is to do everything in my power to accurately calculate the outcome of the war. Allowing any personal biases to affect my work would be a grave disservice to the people of Yan.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: You don't compromise in your duties, and neither do I.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I hope everything goes smoothly...

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: If the outcome is inevitable, it's best not to worry too much about it.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: If you are alone for the Mid-Autumn Festival, come to my home for dinner.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...I will.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: Wait... I just thought of something.

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: Didn't you just ask me who has authority to alter the Academy's records?

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: That did happen once, although it was under extremely unusual circumstances.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You mean...

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: No. I can't say that the records were ever altered. However, if a record has gone missing entirely, then it must have been transferred to another location—

steps.name: Professor Jing
steps.text: Death row, at the Ministry of Justice.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Father is not here?
It's been more than six months since he was last here. The furnishings in the house have not changed, only there are many more symbols symbolizing war on the sand table.
A lone city stands in defiance, the two sides gazing at each other from afar.
Lord Zuo...
A thick, familiar voice rings out from behind.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Uncle Taihe!

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Your... your injuries?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: I was finally able to walk since two weeks ago, albeit with some difficulty. At least I'm no longer bedridden.
Zuo Le stares at Taihe unbelievably, who does not look like the man he remembers.
The wind lifts a corner of his cloak, revealing his thin, withered figure under his wide robe.
Taihe, once a man so strong and sturdy, is now emaciated. It's as if a mere gust of wind could blow him away.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Uncle Taihe...

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Kung fu is merely an external tool. I am, after all, still a monitor censor of the Department of Discipline and Supervision, and there will always be opportunities to realize my aspirations.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: If you continue to dwell on this, Lord Zuo, then you're only underestimating my skills.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Taihe, I know you are no ordinary man. A few injuries aren't enough to stop you!

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: It has been over six months since we last met. You look stronger than before. The General will be pleased.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: By the way, Father is...

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: The General has been in constant meetings with the Sui Regulator and the Ministry of War. He's barely had ten minutes to rest.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The situation...

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: ...Could change in an instant.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Is the court still ready to go to war at all costs?

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Now, after the incident in Dahuang, the bestial Sui is no longer under the Sui Regulator's control.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: There are some minor disagreements between the cabinet and the Six Ministries, but their overall opinion is clear—

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Eliminate the threat once and for all.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: But... the consequences of this war will be...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I heard that one month ago, other Candleholders discovered traces of the convict near Baizao.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: Yes. I heard the same thing.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: The imperial court is on high alert; they've already dispatched several units of Imperial Guards.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: The Imperial Guards...

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: The convict's unpredictability is currently the gravest threat we face.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I have a theory, perhaps...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: There is still another Proxy in Baizao...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: This Proxy is the 'youngest', and the most unique.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: According to the Sui Regulator's observations, in the hundreds of years since he left the tomb, he has never used any of his powers. The Sui Regulator does not know how to deal with him...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: There's only one thing that's a little suspicious—one hundred years ago, after Wang escaped from prison, he came to Baizao and has remained here ever since.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Wang used to frequently interact with other Proxies, so I am afraid that during his current return to Baizao, the lone Proxy who stayed here would also be part of his plan.

steps.name: Taihe
steps.text: What do you plan to do?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I don't know yet, so I'm going to go take a look...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: ...And see for myself.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Phew! Finished!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: What do you think? I've memorized every step, from washing the vegetables to serving the noodles. I can do this all by myself now!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Of course, it's all thanks to Xingzhu for figuring out a genius solution—I just need to dip my hands in ice water for five minutes before kneading the dough, and it comes out fine.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: It looks good, and I can taste the craftsmanship in the dish.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: It'll do, even if it's far from perfect.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: If anyone could cook as well as me after just a few classes, then all my years of study would be in vain.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Hey, I've been working hard for so long, and tomorrow is the big day. Can't you at least say something encouraging?

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: I just don't want you to get a big head... Alright, maybe you're right—a little pep talk might do you good; otherwise, you'd be too scared to cook the minute you meet Mo Bufu.

steps.name: Young Chef
steps.text: Remember: there's nothing to be afraid of. Mo Bufu is old. Show him the power of your youth!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Everything's ready. Let's go win one at Ding Feng Lou tomorrow!
